title: Dupree's records, including Shake Baby
summary: Gardner tries to recall Dupree's hit record, settling on Shake Baby, before Dupree moved to Germany.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Oh, man, that's unbelievable. I mean, I know with Toots, because I used to hang out with Toots a lot and listen to Toots a lot. Play the Jungle Blues. Play the Jungle Blues. Yeah, but I can imagine what Dan Dupree was like. Yeah. That would be like, you know, Professor Longhair.

I think with his voice, big record he had, he came back here to the house. Uh-huh. Not Honey Horse. He had a record out, it made a little noise. I mean, when I say noise, it sold a few records. Mr. Bear?

No. I mean, I'm getting a little bit of a record. See, and the police stopped him, but he didn't have a break tag or something. And he was saying, I'm champion Jack Dupree. Oh, man, I can't think of that number. I'm going to have to call you and tell you about it.
I'm trying to look it up.

But it was one of his big records. He was even kind of big in New Orleans. And that Honey Horse, Shake Baby. Shake Baby? Shake Baby. Okay. Yeah. That was it. That was it. See, I got that record out Shake Baby. That was a big record for him. He got a little recognition. That's before he moved to Germany. And I can say that was another experience that I'm grateful for.
